# S294 — Fix rounds: pause and ask when they make no progress, and pause after round 3 instead of stopping at 8

*Proposed.* A slice whose implementer rounds make no progress no longer loops silently to the round limit. The hard stop at 8 implementer rounds goes away. After round 3 ends red, ork pauses the run into Needs you with one plain question that names the repeated failure and offers three ways on: grant more rounds, change the check, or stop. A round that changed nothing in the worktree and whose check output is byte-identical to the previous round's pauses at once with the same question, without waiting for round 3. Owner decisions, 2026-11-05: the pause is a new pending kind `rounds`, retried with `ork retry RUN [--rounds N]`; a retry grants 2 more rounds by default and the run pauses again if still red, so rounds never stop a run silently (the cap of 4 means round 4 needs the owner's OK); red checks, findings and gate FAILs all count toward round 3; no progress means the worktree content fingerprint and the check log are both unchanged; the cap is an adj key only, with no registry setting.

Owner decision, 2026-11-05: the approval card's `Fix` button is itself the owner's OK. `Fix` refuses only past the current limit (the pause threshold, round 3, plus any rounds a retry granted); within it, the fix round runs at once and never needs a separate `ork retry`.

**Findings:** 2026-11-05, prism-ui: runs ork-20261105-160022-7f6e (U41) and -03e0 (U30) each ran 8 implementer rounds against a check that could not pass (MSB1009 from the wrong directory, S293); from round 2 the implementer reported no change and blamed the check; all 16 check logs are byte-identical. Owner 2026-11-05: '8 fix rounds is too many! More than three should throw some kind of alert or do something different.' Wanted: default cap 4 (DefaultMaxRounds, internal/engine/engine.go:26, not configurable per project or run); pause into Needs you after round 3 with options (more rounds, change the check, stop); pause at once when a round changed nothing and the check output repeats byte for byte. Related: S279, S293. · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:** running the check from the project's subfolder (S293); validating the check command before a run (S295); resuming a stopped run (S296); merging main into a stale worktree before a fix round (S279); a rerun of a flaky check (S239); a per-project or per-run round-limit setting (owner decided 2026-11-05: none); a new daemon notification channel (the TUI bell already rings on a new Needs you row).

## Why

Owner evidence, 2026-11-05 (prism-ui; run records `ork-20261105-160022-7f6e` U41 and `ork-20261105-160022-03e0` U30 under `~/.local/state/ork/runs/`): each run spent 8 implementer rounds on a red check that no code change could fix. The configured check (`dotnet build PrismUi.slnx -c Release && ...`) ran from the worktree root and failed `MSB1009: Project file does not exist` (S293 is the directory fix). From round 2 the implementer reported no change and said the failure was in the check, not the code; ork kept looping until the cap and stopped. Owner, 2026-11-05: "8 fix rounds is too many! More than three should throw some kind of alert or do something different."

Read in the run records (2026-11-05): both `run.json` files say `state: stopped`, `round: 8`, reason "the round limit of 8 implementer rounds was reached", 8 `checks[]` rows all `ok: false`. All 16 `checks-N.log` files of the two runs have the same MD5 (each holds one `MSB1009` line), so rule (c) below would have paused both runs after round 2. The implementer reports were not read; "No change this round" is from the owner's account.

What the code at HEAD of main shows (read 2026-11-05):

- `DefaultMaxRounds = 8` (`internal/engine/engine.go:24-26`), used through `Deps.maxRounds()` (`engine.go:79-84`; `Deps.MaxRounds`, `engine.go:59`, "0 means DefaultMaxRounds"). It is not configurable per project or per run: the only non-test setter is `initRunManager` copying `d.cfg.Engine` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:157-160`), and only tests set `MaxRounds` (`internal/engine/engine_test.go:461`, `round_test.go:192`, `internal/engine/approval_test.go:173`). The registry, `ork projects set` and `ork run` have no round flag (`internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:356` lists the set flags).
- `bumpRound` (`internal/engine/states.go:129-141`) is the one place a red result starts another implementer round: checks (`checks`, `states.go:163-179`), review and architect findings, and gate FAILs all call it. At the limit it calls `e.stop` (`engine.go:539-563`), which ends the run (`runrec.StateStopped`) and closes the ledger run as failed. `Fix` on the approval card (`internal/engine/approval.go:168`) refuses at the same limit (`approval.go:179-180`).
- The check log is `checks-ROUND.log` in the run directory, written by `runChecks` (`states.go:191-248`) from the check command output and `slicer check --json`; `checks[]` records round, command, ok and seconds, not a hash.
- A worktree fingerprint already exists for read-only roles: `treeStatus` (`internal/engine/round.go:99-107`, `git status --porcelain`, adj `role.readonly-fingerprint`). It does not see content changes to a file that was already modified, so it is not enough on its own for "no change this round".
- The model for a pause that a retry grants past: the budget pause (`runrec.PendingBudget`, `internal/runrec/record.go:144`; `overBudget` and the grant in `runRound`, `round.go:150-200`; adj 127 `run.budget-resume`: "retry grants exactly one more role round ... MaxRounds stays"). This slice changes what adj 127 says about `MaxRounds`, so it needs a new adj key (owner decided 2026-11-05: the key only, no registry setting; the owner files it).
- How a pause shows: `ork status` prints the pending reason then `; next: ork retry ID` for any non-question pause (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1300-1322`). The TUI lists paused runs under Needs you and rings the bell when a project's Needs you count rises (`internal/tui/model.go:1123-1225`; the bell function is set at `model.go:225-226`; silenced by the registry bell setting). The daemon has no alert path of its own: it only notifies subscribers that the snapshot changed (`MethodSnapshotChanged`, `internal/daemon/subscribe.go:85`). An `Ask` with options is today only answered with `ork answer` (`PendingQuestion`, `runs.go:990-1012`).
- Changing the check while the run is paused: a paused run is unfinished (`runrec.IsFinal`, `internal/runrec/record.go:39`), so `ork projects set --check` is refused (`internal/daemon/handlers.go:587-593`); S265's Q5 answer (2026-11-03) keeps `--check` refused while runs are unfinished. A started engine also keeps the project it started with (`internal/daemon/runs.go:578-579`), so a plain retry would not see a new check. "Change the check" at this pause therefore means: stop the run, set the check, then resume it with `ork retry` (S296). Until S296 lands, it means stop and a new `ork run`.
- Tests that set `MaxRounds` and must keep their meaning: `TestTheRoundLimitStopsARedLoop` (`engine_test.go:459`), `TestAutomaticShapeRetryDoesNotUseARound` (`round_test.go:190`) and `TestFixActionAtTheRoundLimitRefusesWithoutStopping` (`approval_test.go:171`).

Related: S279 (a round that fails twice on the same outside finding uses this slice's `rounds` pause instead of stopping the run; owner decision 2026-11-05), S293, S239, S255, S282.

## Implement

1. Tests first. Confirm each fails for the reason given.
2. Replace the hard stop at `DefaultMaxRounds = 8` with a pause after round 3 (the first pause; name the constant to match). Keep `Deps.MaxRounds` for tests as the round after which the first pause comes (0 means 3), and change `TestTheRoundLimitStopsARedLoop` (`engine_test.go:459`) to expect the pause. Add no registry field (owner decided 2026-11-05).
3. Fingerprint the worktree after each implementer round: tracked content and untracked names, so an edit to an already modified file counts as a change. Store it on the implementer's role record. Hash each check log and store it on its `checks[]` row.
4. In `bumpRound` for `Kind == "checks"`: when this round's tree fingerprint equals the previous round's and this check log hash equals the previous check's, pause at once (rule c). Apply rule (c) only to checks feedback; findings and FAILs keep their paths.
5. In `bumpRound`, when the round that just ended is round 3 and the result is red (any feedback kind; owner decided 2026-11-05), pause instead of starting round 4 (rule b). The pending reason is one line: `round 3 ended red: <step> failed (<last line of the log>); ork retry ID grants 2 more rounds; to change the check, ork stop ID, set it, then ork retry ID; or ork stop ID`. The "change the check" path needs S296's resume of a stopped run; before S296 lands it ends in a new `ork run` (see Why). Set `pending.state` to `implement` and keep the feedback, so a retry continues with it.
6. A retry of this pause grants 2 rounds by default (`--rounds N`) the way a budget retry grants one (`round.go:194-200`): the next pause comes after round `round + N`, held in the record so a daemon restart keeps it. Share the record field and the `--rounds` wire field with S296 (see Files).
7. `Fix` on the approval card (`internal/engine/approval.go:179-180`) compares with the current limit (the pause threshold plus the record's grant) instead of `MaxRounds`; it refuses only past that limit and needs no retry (owner decision 2026-11-05).
8. Status: the `next:` hint for this kind is `ork retry ID [--rounds N] or ork stop ID`. The TUI needs no change: a paused run is a Needs you row and the bell rings (verify in the test that the TUI row source sees `pending` set).
9. Docs and CHANGELOG in the same diff. The owner files the adj key (for example `run.round-limit`) that supersedes the `MaxRounds` clause of adj 127.
